_comment: What this list is: permission-prompt reduction for the commands this project runs
constantly, narrowed to the actual invocations. What it is NOT: a sandbox or a
security boundary. Rules are prefix-matched, so the earlier `Bash(uv run *)` and
`Bash(python3 *)` entries matched `uv run git push` and any Python subprocess --
an outward action reached through an allowlisted interpreter (cross-model review,
round 1). Narrowing removes that specific hole and keeps the blast radius small,
but `Bash(scripts/*)` still covers finish-item.sh --delete-remote, which pushes a
branch deletion. Nothing here can stop a cooperating agent from reaching the
network; git push, gh pr create and gh pr merge are absent by intent, and the real
boundary on outward actions is the operator. Add exact commands as they come up
rather than widening a prefix back out to an interpreter.
